Subtitle

Drop videos or audio files, press Start. Subtitles appear only while someone speaks.

Setting up

Options

Results
Ready.

Merge

One video plus audio and/or subtitle files → one .joined.mkv next to the video. Lossless: nothing is re-encoded. Without an audio file the video keeps its own sound; tracks are language-tagged from names like Movie.de.srt.

Files

Add one video and the tracks that should go into it.

Split

Subtitles miss the voice? Export every channel of the audio track as its own WAV (Movie.ch00.wav, Movie.ch01.wav, …) next to the file and listen which one carries the speech. Then choose that channel under Audio channel on the Subtitle page. Nothing is transcribed here.

Files

Add the files whose channels you want to hear separately.

Settings

This page is built from SuperSubtitler_Config.ini itself. Before saving, SuperSubtitler checks the new values — a value it would refuse is not written. The previous file is kept as .bak.

Subtitle cleaner

One term per line; any subtitle containing it is removed (ads, hallucinated junk). A line starting with = only removes a subtitle that is exactly that text. Lines starting with # are notes.

About

This window never transcribes anything itself: it starts SuperSubtitler.exe and shows what it reports.

What it puts on your disk

Everything lives in this folder, nothing in the registry: ffmpeg.exe/ffprobe.exe, Python\ (engine), whisper\models\ (speech models), the two settings files and SuperSubtitlerGUI.window (this window's size and theme). Delete the folder and it is gone.

Licence and credits

SuperSubtitler and this window: free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 only — free for everyone, at home or at work. Speech recognition: faster-whisper (MIT) running OpenAI's Whisper models (MIT). Audio/video: FFmpeg (SuperSubtitler's own lean LGPL build; sources in the runtime-v1 release). Window: Wails (MIT) on Microsoft WebView2.
